analysis.title: Signal over noise: Agentic AI—redrawing the AI value pool
key_insights: UBS CIO argues AI agents are becoming a layer between consumers, businesses and platforms, changing both the scale of compute demand and how value is created and captured across the digital economy.

The shift puts pressure on business models built around human interaction, mainly digital advertising and seat-based enterprise software. It favors companies that control infrastructure, trusted data, execution layers and differentiated AI capabilities.

UBS recommends broadening AI exposure beyond today's dominant technology platforms, because value may migrate from established internet franchises to new entrants, infrastructure providers and businesses less exposed to interface disruption.

Markets have overreacted in the AI ROI debate, rewarding potential beneficiaries and assigning near-zero terminal value to businesses seen as vulnerable. Software was sold broadly on fears that agentic tools displace SaaS, and cybersecurity sold off on advanced-cyber-capability models before reversing.
The cybersecurity selloff reversed because the same model capabilities expand the range and sophistication of attacks, which raises demand for security services.

If agents become the primary way to access the web, users bypass interfaces built to capture attention. That weakens the link between attention and monetization for businesses reliant on direct human engagement.

OpenRouter reported 790 trillion tokens in October 2026, up 37% from September and almost 25 times January's volume. Agentic API keys were 76% of tokens versus 8% a year earlier, and agentic volume was about 7.2 times human-classified volume. UBS notes OpenRouter's traffic is tilted toward software-development automation.

UBS estimates token consumption will rise from about 150-200 billion tokens per minute now to more than 2.5 trillion by 2030. API calls are expected to be about 85% of consumption, with agentic workloads taking a disproportionate share.

Agent tool adoption is fast: OpenClaw passed 100,000 GitHub stars in January 2026 and 250,000 by March, becoming the most-starred software project on the platform in about 60 days. UBS notes stars measure developer interest, not active usage.

Muse recorded an estimated 10.2 million US downloads in its first 40 days, almost three times ChatGPT's mobile app at 3.7 million over the same period. Meta reported strong engagement and sought higher payment-processing credit limits.

For digital advertising, delegated purchasing can bypass the touchpoints where platforms monetize attention. Agents compare specifications, prices and availability without a search page or retailer visit, which shifts value toward machine-readable product data, real-time inventory and purchasing integrations.

For enterprise software, agents that reconcile invoices, route tickets or call systems directly reduce the need for added human seats and weaken the dashboard's role. Per-seat pricing links revenue to employee count and is exposed. Software providers can stay essential by supplying trusted data, business logic, permissions and execution, and by moving to usage or outcome pricing.

In 3Q26 earnings, Amazon and Alphabet both beat cloud revenue expectations (AWS +39% y/y, Google Cloud +103% y/y) while advertising revenue missed forecasts. Amazon's ad slowdown was mostly event timing and comparisons.

Alphabet's Search revenue grew 12% y/y and search-query growth hit a five-year high, but revenue growth decelerated. UBS says AI Mode queries, which monetize at a lower rate than conventional searches, weighed meaningfully on growth, which illustrates cannibalization risk.

UBS does not take an outright negative view of Alphabet. It points to vertical integration across TPUs, cloud, proprietary models and applications such as Waymo, plus paid assistant subscriptions and enterprise AI services, as routes to offset search pressure.

UBS says the speed of AI disruption is underappreciated by markets, but does not recommend abandoning large-cap tech. It expects market expansion combined with redistribution of revenue from existing profit pools, creating leaders and laggards.

UBS says the greatest pressure could fall on digital businesses reliant on human attention, interfaces or per-user software. Because these models are concentrated in the largest tech companies, this creates portfolio concentration risk.

UBS sees physical-economy businesses as comparatively insulated, and names compute, power infrastructure, security and differentiated AI applications as ways to participate. It suggests equal-weighted equity exposure to reduce mega-cap concentration and add smaller companies and new entrants.

market_movers.rationale: UBS CIO calls Alphabet the clearest illustration of tension between a strong AI asset base and pressure on search advertising economics, citing AI Mode cannibalization. It does not take an outright negative view.
AWS grew 39% y/y and beat cloud expectations. Advertising missed, which UBS attributes largely to event timing and comparison effects.

sector_views.rationale: Delegated agent purchasing can bypass the touchpoints where platforms monetize human attention. Agentic discovery reduces conventional advertising opportunities.
Agents reduce the need for added human-operated seats and weaken the dashboard interface. Per-seat pricing is most exposed, and providers must move to usage or outcome pricing.
Agentic workloads drive token demand toward more than 2.5 trillion per minute by 2030, and infrastructure providers are named as alternative ways to participate.
Advanced AI cyber capabilities expand the range and sophistication of attacks, which raises demand for security services.
Comparatively insulated from direct interface disruption, as the value pool shifts.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 (already reported): Amazon and Alphabet both beat cloud revenue expectations. AWS grew 39% y/y and Google Cloud grew 103% y/y. Advertising revenue fell short of forecasts at both companies.

Alphabet 3Q26 (reported): Search revenue grew 12% y/y and search-query growth reached a five-year high, but total revenue growth decelerated. UBS attributes part of the slowdown to AI Mode queries monetizing at lower rates than conventional search.
Amazon 3Q26 (reported): UBS says the advertising slowdown was largely driven by specific event timing and comparison effects.

trade_ideas.description: Move to equal-weighted equity exposure to reduce mega-cap concentration and add smaller companies and potential new entrants
trade_ideas.rationale: AI disruption may redistribute revenue away from large internet franchises, which are concentrated in the largest tech companies.

risk_factors: Value migrates away from established internet franchises whose revenues depend on human attention, interfaces or per-seat software.
Cannibalization of search advertising as AI-mediated and agentic interfaces shift activity to lower-monetizing interactions, even as overall usage rises.
Portfolio concentration risk, since attention-based and per-seat business models sit mainly in the largest technology companies.
Markets overreact to AI monetization narratives, which causes sharp reversals such as the cybersecurity selloff.
OpenRouter token data is tilted toward software-development automation, and GitHub stars measure interest rather than usage.

tension_points.bull_case: Big tech has infrastructure, distribution, data and customer relationships. Alphabet's vertical integration across TPUs, cloud, models and Waymo, plus paid assistant and enterprise AI subscriptions, could offset pressure on existing economics. AI expands output and creates new revenue pools.
tension_points.bear_case: Agents intermediate discovery and transactions and bypass ad touchpoints and seat-based dashboards. Alphabet's AI Mode queries monetize below conventional search and weighed on 3Q26 revenue growth, while some AI revenue is redistributed from existing profit pools.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further evidence that growth in lower-monetizing AI queries keeps decelerating Alphabet's revenue, or that agents become the primary means of accessing the web and users bypass advertising interfaces.
